Input syntax¶

input.txt describes the input as “a kind of NAMELIST free format”. It is close to the GAMESS-US format: keywords are grouped, and each group starts with $name and ends with $end. This chapter covers the rules that apply to all groups. The individual keywords are in the input reference.

A complete input for an NH3 optimization, adapted from the KNC wiki FAQ:

$system mem=512 disk=-512 path=/tmp $end
$control
 task=optimize
 theory=dft
 basis=/opt/priroda/basis.in
$end
$optimize tol=1e-5 steps=100 $end
$molecule
 charge=0 mult=1
 z-matrix
 set=L1
   7
   1    1    1.02672223
   1    1    1.02672140    2    104.150240
   1    1    1.02671372    2    104.144601   -3    104.150290
$end

Groups¶

A group starts with $ followed by the group name and ends with $end. It may sit on one line or span several:

$scf conv=1e-7 $end

$scf
 procedure=bfgs
 convergence=1e-7
$end

Inside a group, keyword=value pairs are separated by spaces or line breaks, and several pairs can share a line (theory=qm_n3 basis=qm.in). Blank lines inside a group are allowed.

The order of the groups does not matter, and neither does the order of keywords within a group. The exception is $molecule, whose contents are ordered data. (The KNC wiki FAQ also lists $Energy, but version 25 reads it with the same keyword reader as the other groups.)

Groups you do not need can be left out; most keywords have sensible defaults. input.txt advises changing only what the problem requires.

Two groups can also share a line: $scf conv=1e-7,1e-3 $end $grid acc=1e-9 $end sets both values in version 25. Inputs in the sources normally start each group on a new line, which is easier to read.

Keywords¶

Case¶

Group names, keyword names and keyword values are case-insensitive: $System and $system, theory=riDFT and theory=ridft, functional=pbe and functional=PBE are the same. File names are the exception, because Linux file names are case-sensitive. This applies to basis=, save=, path= and other file names, such as file= in $dynamic and $uniq.

Abbreviations¶

Within a group, a keyword can be shortened to a prefix. The example in input.txt is mem for memory. Inputs in the sources use, among others:

Short form

Keyword

mem=

$system memory

conv=, iter=, proc=

$scf convergence, iterations, procedure

func=

$dft functional

acc=, accur=

$grid accuracy

tol=, cart=, val=

$optimize tolerance, cartesian, value

disp=

$d2edr2 displace

nuc=

$control nucleus

rout=

$integral routine

Keywords belong to their group. The same name can mean different things in different groups: steps in $optimize is the maximum number of optimization cycles, while steps in $d2edr2 selects displacement steps of a numerical Hessian.

Warning

A prefix must stay unambiguous within its group. In $scf, co matches both convergence and core; in version 25, $scf co=1e-7 $end stopped with unknown name e-7, a message that does not point to the cause. In inputs you keep or share, prefer the full keyword names; they are also easier to search for.

Do not give the same keyword twice in one group, even in different spellings. In version 6, an $optimize group with both step= and steps= took the maximum number of steps from step.

A misspelled or unknown keyword name stops the run right after the basis-set echo, with a message naming the group and the keyword:

*** error in '$scf' : unknown name nosuchkeyword

Only groups that the task reads are checked. In version 25, an unknown keyword in $optimize stopped an optimization (unknown name coordinated) but was ignored in an energy run, which does not read $optimize. A clean energy run therefore does not prove that the rest of the input is correct.

The same message can appear for a keyword you spelled correctly. In version 25, convergence= with a single value, followed by iterations=, stops the run with the name of iterations cut short:

  • $scf convergence=1e-7 iterations=250 $end printed unknown name terations on the machine of the first test rounds, also with the two keywords on separate lines;

  • the same input printed unknown name erations in later runs of the p4_d executable on another machine. There the message was the same for every value tried (1e-5, 1e-6, 1e-7, 1e-10, 0.000001, 1.0e-6, and 1e-6, with a trailing comma), and iter=50 gave unknown name er.

Other keywords after a one-value convergence= were read normally (procedure, restrict, xmax, diagm, temperature, fraction, core, eemin, aw), but n1= stopped the run with no '$end' found, 'convergence'. The problem disappears when convergence gets both of its values (convergence=1e-6,1e-3 iterations=50) or comes after iterations. Give convergence both values, or put it last in the group; see $scf convergence.

Values¶

Scalars

Integers (steps=100), reals in plain or exponent notation (trust=0.2, tol=1e-5) and words (task=optimize). A sign is allowed: charge=+1.

Lists

Values separated by commas, for keywords that take several numbers: tol=1e-5,1e-4, mem=2048,256, temperature=203, 223, 248, 298. Spaces after the commas are allowed, and some lists are also written with spaces between groups of values (fix=1,1,2,0,0 3,2,1,4,3). If you give fewer values than the keyword holds, the rest keep their defaults: $scf conv=1e-10 sets only the SCF threshold and leaves the CP-SCF threshold at 1e-3.

Indexed arrays

name(i)=a,b,… assigns values to an array starting at element i and leaves the other elements unchanged. $guess na(85)=86,85 $end sets element 85 of na to 86 and element 86 to 85, which swaps two orbitals. The same form is used for $optimize value (val(5)=2.0,2.1), $nmr standard (standard(6)=181.9921) and $atoms core.

Flag strings

$control print takes a string of options, each switched on with + or off with -: print=+vectors+molden, print=-internals+molden. The leading + may be omitted (print=charges+bonds).

Quoted strings

A file name or path may be put in double quotes. The quotes are optional: basis="3z.bas" and basis=basis.in both work, as does path="/scratch/priroda". Use the straight ASCII double quote ". Typographic quotes break the name, and two single quotes do not count as a double quote: basis=''3z.bas'' fails with error opening file ''3z.bas''. Avoid spaces and non-ASCII characters in file names, directory names and the host name.

The $molecule group¶

$molecule is read as ordered data rather than as keyword pairs:

  1. charge= and mult= (spin multiplicity 2S+1), both optional, with defaults 0 and 1;

  2. one of the words cartesian or z-matrix;

  3. one line per atom, optionally preceded by set= lines that choose the basis set for the atoms that follow.

The first items may share the opening line:

$molecule charge=0 mult=1 cartesian
 set=L1
  8    0.000000    0.000000    0.117300
  1    0.000000    0.757200   -0.469200
  1    0.000000   -0.757200   -0.469200
$end

Each atom line begins with the atomic number written as an integer. Cartesian coordinates are in Å unless unit=b is given. The Z-matrix forms, mixed Cartesian and Z-matrix input, isotope masses and per-atom basis sets are described in the $molecule reference.

Several $molecule blocks¶

Some tasks read more than one $molecule group from one input:

  • task=transit, task=saddle and task=path take two blocks, the start and the end structure. The atoms must be numbered the same way in both. task=saddle is not the same as $optimize saddle=1, the transition-state search from a stored Hessian. This two-block input was reported for versions 8–9 and has not been tested on version 25.

  • task=uniq takes any number of blocks and filters out duplicate structures; the official example has 157.

These tasks are undocumented; see $control task and $uniq.

Text outside groups¶

Everything outside a $name … $end group is ignored. There is no documented comment character, but this rule serves the same purpose, and the official example inputs use it to switch input off:

  • Delete the $ to disable a whole group. integral dir=1 $end in the official 2023–2025 example inputs is plain text, not an $integral group.

  • Move keywords after $end to disable them. In the example below, v= and h= are outside $dynamic and have no effect.

  • Keep notes after $end. Helper scripts append result lines such as Energy = … after the $molecule group, where they do no harm.

integral dir=1 $end
$dynamic
 e=0.001
 d=0.03
 n=1000,100
$end
 v=500.0
 h=0.1
$molecule charge=0 mult=1 cartesian
 set=L1
  8    0.000000    0.000000    0.117300
  1    0.000000    0.757200   -0.469200
  1    0.000000   -0.757200   -0.469200
$end
 Energy =   -76.36539137

In version 25 a line of text before the first group and a disabled group with its leftover $end (integral dir=1 $end) are both ignored: the result is identical to the same input without them. Text inside a group is parsed as keywords, so do not put notes there.

A group opened with & instead of $ is ignored like any other text: in version 25, &dft func=BLYP $end left the functional at PBE, with no message. Always use $.

Appending results of earlier runs¶

Priroda writes reusable results into the main output file. Each such line carries a prefix, for example eng> or num>. Strip the prefix and append the lines to the next input. The program has no separate restart file for these data; SCF orbitals are the exception, saved with $control save.

$Energy from eng> lines¶

A run prints its energy and dipole, plus the gradient when one is computed and, after task=hessian, the Hessian, as an $Energy group on lines prefixed with eng>:

eng>$Energy
eng> E=-2.894457077327e+04
eng> D= 0.00000000e+00  0.00000000e+00  0.00000000e+00
eng> G= 3.53877831e-09  1.65504544e-08 -3.64771621e-07
eng>   -1.31128901e-07 -6.73350427e-09 -2.19780956e-06
eng>    1.27590122e-07 -9.81695012e-09  2.56258122e-06
eng>$end

To reuse it, remove the prefix and append the block to the end of the next input, after $molecule:

sed -n 's/^eng>//p' mol.out >> mol.in

The ge script on the official site does the same. When the output contains a NUMERICAL AND ANALYTICAL GRADIENT section, it ignores everything before that section.

Warning

An optimization prints an eng> block at every step, and the command above appends all of them. Append only the block you need, normally the one from a task=hessian run. If the input holds several $Energy groups, the program uses the last one, even when an earlier one matches the geometry.

A stored Hessian is required by $optimize saddle=1 and task=irc. It also helps difficult minimizations, and it lets you redo the vibrational analysis or the thermochemistry without recomputing.

num> lines¶

Partial results of a numerical calculation are printed on lines prefixed with num>. There are two uses:

  • A numerical Hessian split over several runs with $d2edr2 steps. Collect the num> lines of all partial outputs into one input, add $d2edr2 steps=-1 $end, and run once more:

    grep -h "^num>" mol.out1 mol.out2 mol.out3 mol.out4 | sed 's/^num>//' >> mol.in

    The lines hold numbered $Energy000, $Energy001, … groups, one per displaced geometry. The combining run does no SCF of its own. The command given in input.txt, sed "s/\.*num>//g", leaves the file names that grep adds for several files at the start of each line; use grep -h as above.

  • Raman intensities. A task=dipole run writes num> lines; append them to the input of a task=hessian run, and the Raman A. and Raman D. columns of the frequency table are filled in.

Optimized geometry from MOL> lines¶

After OPTIMIZATION CONVERGED, the final geometry is printed as a ready-made $molecule group on lines prefixed with MOL>. Strip the prefix to continue from that geometry. The gm script on the official site replaces the $molecule group of the input with it. Because gm replaces everything from $molecule to the end of the file, keep $molecule as the last group of your inputs. Anything appended after it, including an $Energy group with a Hessian, is deleted by gm; append such blocks again afterwards.

An optimization that runs out of steps prints no MOL> lines in version 25. The geometry of each step is printed on lines prefixed with lowercase mol>; the block from the last step is the geometry to restart from. gm finds neither MOL> lines nor an input echo in such an output and stops with mol?, so strip the last mol> block by hand.

Common mistakes¶

Non-integer atomic numbers

25.0 or 8.0 instead of 25 or 8 in $molecule. The atom lines are read as a stream of numbers, so the rest of the group shifts. In version 25 this gives no error at all: water written with 8.0 and 1.0 ran as an oxygen atom plus three empty centres with Z=0, and printed a meaningless energy. Older versions were reported to stop with illegal charge/multiplicity. Check the formula: line near the top of the output. Element symbols are not accepted either: in version 25, water written with O and H stopped after molecule input: '' with the line 'o' ?.

Typographic quotes

Word processors and some web pages turn " into curly or angle quotes, which break file names in basis= and path=. Retype them as straight quotes.

Two task= lines

A second task= line does not start a second job; in version 6, users reported that only the first task ran. task=optimize+hessian is the only combination the program understands. Run other sequences as separate jobs.

Windows line endings (CRLF)

The run stops in $molecule with molecule input: '' followed by a garbled ' ?matrix or ?rtesian. Convert the file with dos2unix; see Installing and running.

Misspelled task or theory name

Gives no error. An unknown task= value sets up the run and stops quietly after the SCF and grid settings; an unknown theory= value runs Hartree–Fock, with the misspelled name in the summary box. Check the Theoretical Method line and that the output goes on to an SCF.

Hybrid functional without theory=ridft

Older versions ran but gave wrong results. With theory=dft, version 25 stops after the basis-set echo with no message in the output file (stderr shows only MPI_Abort); with theory=tddft it still runs without the exact exchange and gives wrong energies. See $control theory.

basis4.in without four=1

The relativistic basis file needs four=1 in $control. Without it, version 25 stops right after the line Basis set input: with the single line 1?.

More input problems, with their exact error messages, are listed in The input is not read, or is read wrongly.
